items.followUp: Explain how biology is related to physics and geography through two interdisciplinary sciences.

rubric.why: Award for naming biophysics and explaining its connection between biology and physics.
rubric.description: Biophysics applies the principles of physics to biological phenomena.
rubric.how: Look for biophysics linked to physics and biological phenomena or living organisms.

rubric.why: Award for naming biochemistry and relating it to the chemistry of organisms.
rubric.description: Biochemistry studies the chemical composition and reactions of organisms.
rubric.how: Look for biochemistry linked to chemical composition or reactions in organisms.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the mathematical or statistical study of biological data.
rubric.description: Biometry applies mathematics and statistics to biological data and processes.
rubric.how: Look for biometry linked to mathematical or statistical methods applied to biology.

rubric.why: Award for naming biogeography and explaining its focus on where organisms occur.
rubric.description: Biogeography studies the geographical distribution of organisms.
rubric.how: Look for biogeography linked to the distribution of organisms across geographical areas.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the economic relationship between biology and organisms or biological resources.
rubric.description: Bioeconomics studies organisms or biological resources from an economic point of view.
rubric.how: Look for bioeconomics linked to the economic importance or use of organisms or biological resources.

modelAnswer: Biophysics applies the principles of physics to biological phenomena.
Biochemistry studies the chemical composition of organisms and the chemical reactions occurring in them.
Biometry applies mathematical and statistical methods to biological data and processes.
Biogeography studies the geographical distribution of organisms.
Bioeconomics studies organisms and biological resources from an economic point of view.

items.followUp: Give one example each of a quantitative and a qualitative observation.

rubric.why: Award for defining a quantitative observation as one involving numerical data or measurement.
rubric.description: A quantitative observation is expressed in numbers or measurements.
rubric.how: Look for quantitative linked to numbers, numerical data, counting, or measurement.

rubric.why: Award for defining a qualitative observation as describing qualities or characteristics.
rubric.description: A qualitative observation describes qualities or characteristics rather than giving a numerical measurement.
rubric.how: Look for qualitative linked to a description of qualities or characteristics.

modelAnswer: A quantitative observation is based on measurement or counting and is expressed in numbers.
A qualitative observation describes qualities or characteristics without expressing them as numbers.
